content.prompt:
The points $P,Q,R,S$ are on the unit circle. $O$ is the origin.
Find the exact coordinates of $P,Q,R,S$.

answer.worked:
On the unit circle, coordinates are $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ for the directed angle $\theta$ from the positive $x$-axis. Read each directed angle from the diagram.
$$\begin{align*}P&:\ \theta=-60^\circ\\P&=(\cos(-60^\circ),\sin(-60^\circ))=\left(\frac12,-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\Q&:\ \theta=270^\circ-30^\circ=240^\circ\\Q&=(\cos240^\circ,\sin240^\circ)=\left(-\frac12,-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\R&:\ \theta=180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ\\R&=(\cos135^\circ,\sin135^\circ)=\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)\\S&:\ \theta=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ\\S&=(\cos60^\circ,\sin60^\circ)=\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\end{align*}$$
